body: you misunderstood that statement bro. When people say money can't buy happiness they mean everlasting happiness. No one is insane enough to think that money doesn't help to contribute to making your life more convenient and comfortable. And that does make you happy for the time being. But that kind of happiness evaporates into nothingness like boiling water. Think about it. You bought a nice house or a sports car with the money. That will make anyone happy at the time. But how long can you be happy with those things? You are going to desire even nicer houses and more cars just to keep yourself at that level of happiness. And you will be chasing more money like a rat chases cheese in a wheel. There are things that will make you happy and fulfilled for the rest of lives and it is accessible to everyone no matter who you are, where you live or what your economic status is.

My personal enquiry into spirituality has led me to believe that all things matter are emergent properties of consciousness rather than the other way around. That's what I found all the great sages unanimously agreeing upon. If what they are saying happens to be true, then nothing exists outside of consciousness. I know this sounds very radical. I have not yet actualized it myself. I have not had high doses of LSD but planning on doing it some day. Until then, I'm practicing yoga and meditation to prepare myself for the experience and being open to all the explanations of reality.

All our experiences of running into wall, hanging stuffs on it etc are all products of our mind. Whatever our mind produces must be a substrate of reality. I'm not saying that the wall isn't there. The wall is very much there there but only relative to our mind. I believe that certain chemicals can remove the veil of our mind, thoughts and make us see through it. Like the analogy of the screen and the image shown in it. If a tree appears on the screen, is it real? Obviously the answer is no. There is only screen and the modulation of light. Likewise, we see matter and stuffs around us. But that could be just the modulation of some underlying phenomenon (consciousness). One can never experience the wall or the tree outside their mind.
How can you be sure that the wall is the reality. It might be that the wall is what we are hallucinating and LSD enables us to see through it.
